description: VT 15% (expanding, t-1) + DD 8/20 brake overlay on CR08+D01 crowding defense base. Tighter VT + tighter DD vs S5.

gate0_pit.c2_same_day_circular: PASS - vt_lagged = c(1.0, head(vt_scalar, -1)); dd_lag = c(0, dd_pct[-n_f])
gate0_pit.c5_overlay_t_minus_1: PASS - both VT and DD use t-1
gate0_pit.c9_vt_dd_same_day: PASS - VT uses vt_lagged, DD uses dd_lag

gate1_performance.assessment: FAIL - SR 0.598 below 1.0. CAGR 6.25% is the lowest in the family (vs 7.98% base). MDD 23.75% is the best in the family and within 25% target, but at extreme CAGR sacrifice. IR -0.161 is the most negative = worst benchmark underperformance. The tighter VT (15%) aggressively scales down exposure, crushing returns.

gate3_role_honesty.assessment: Diversifier role honest. IR -0.161 confirms strategy cannot serve as core_alpha.

gate4_statistical.assessment: FAIL - OOS retention 23.0% = severe degradation. Alpha trend ratio 0.288 (recent 3Y SR 0.172 vs full 0.598) = alpha nearly exhausted. Tighter overlays do not fix alpha decay -- they merely compress vol, making the low SR appear slightly better via lower denominator.

gate5_ff5.assessment: Not run. SR 0.598 makes FF5 alpha almost certainly insignificant.

s3_orthogonality_review.assessment: POOR - Inherited from base. Factor redundancy unaddressed.

mutation_comparison.vs_m2: M3 achieves lower MDD (23.75% vs 23.89%) but at much worse CAGR (6.25% vs 6.75%) and SR (0.598 vs 0.646). Tighter VT target (15% vs no-VT in M2) is the primary difference.
mutation_comparison.vs_s5: M3 uses tighter VT (15% vs 18%) and tighter DD (8/20 vs 7/22). Achieves 3pp better MDD (23.75% vs 26.76%) but 1.08pp worse CAGR. Net effect: marginally better risk control at disproportionate return cost.
mutation_comparison.assessment: M3 is the most conservative variant. Best MDD (23.75%) but worst CAGR (6.25%) and most negative IR (-0.161). The aggressive vol targeting reduces exposure to the point where the already-weak alpha is nearly extinguished.

rejection_reasons: Factor redundancy: CR08-D01 corr=0.943 (inherited, fundamental flaw)
Lowest CAGR in family: 6.25% (tighter overlays crush already-weak alpha)
Tighter overlays do not fix insufficient base alpha -- they only compress returns
overall_verdict.summary: STR_1422_s5_m3 (VT15+DD8/20) is PIT-clean but the most conservative -- and most return-destructive -- variant. Tightening VT to 15% and DD to 8/20 achieves the family's best MDD (23.75%) but at extreme cost: CAGR drops to 6.25% (lowest), IR to -0.161 (most negative). This confirms L-631 insight: no overlay parameterization can rescue a signal with 0.943 factor redundancy and 0.633 base SR. The tighter the overlay, the more it exposes the core problem -- there is not enough alpha to survive any meaningful risk management.
